thread:
olivia-support: FYI NimbleRx reported intermittent 429s and 600–1200ms tail latencies on their dedicated pool since 09:40 UTC. They say baseline QPS ~180, peak bursts ~750 for 30–90s.
olivia-support: Also seeing some auth failures (invalid_token) around the same windows and one billing alert for unexpected overage.
mike-sre: copy. can you paste sample request IDs and time windows? I want to match with agent traces.
olivia-support: Pasted from customer: request ids: rq_8f3a12, rq_8f3a6b, rq_8f3b00. Windows: 09:40:12–09:41:45 and 10:02:05–10:03:22 UTC.
raj-eng: thanks. initial theory: pool was right at capacity for their baseline (3 GPUs) and autoscale config has cooldown 120s + max burst 1 extra slab. bursts of 750 QPS likely outstrip one-slab bump. noisy neighbour could amplify preemption.
kevin-eng-runtime: I pulled task metrics — during 09:40 window their per-GPU token throughput hit ~62% sustained but scheduler queue shot up. KV cache hit rate dropped 18% (lots of cold prefixes).
mike-sre: KV cache drop explains tail latency. warmup missing. do we have warmup policy for Dedicated?
raj-eng: their Dedicated pool was created with default warmup=false (customer flag). they also disabled prefix caching cuz of sensitive prompts.
anna-product: from product side, customer expects 99th latency <500ms and <2% 429s. currently they report ~4.8% 429s during bursts.
olivia-support: customer is asking for remediation now — asked if we can add headroom or change their autoscale.
kevin-eng-runtime: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) temporarily add +1 slab (adds ~2 GPUs) 2) reduce cooldown to 30s for this pool 3) enable safe warmup with opt-in hashed prefix caching (keeps plaintext out of cache).
raj-eng: agree. also recommend target utilization of 55–65% per GPU for production bursty customers. their current config targeted 75% which is too aggressive for unpredictable spikes.
mike-sre: created a quick run: /runbooks/support/nimblerx-capacity-1712345678 (internal link) with steps. applying +1 slab now, will monitor.
sre-bot: deploy: capacity-scaler updated for pool nimble-rx-pool by mike-sre at 2024-04-26T10:05:12Z :white_check_mark:
kevin-eng-runtime: after +1 slab we saw queue drop and 95th latency move from 1.1s -> 420ms in test replay. still see ~1% auth_invalid spikes — likely caused by their token rotation timing.
olivia-support: customer did a token rotation at ~10:01 — they confirmed. can we surface guidance?
raj-eng: yes: advise rolling token rotation with short overlap (reuse previous token for 5m) and avoid simultaneous multi-worker rotation. also implement client-side exponential backoff for 429s with jitter.
anna-product: can we offer a short-term credit for their billing overage while we stabilize? looks like they were charged for extra tokens during bursts.
mike-sre: flagging billing team. billing-alert-id: bill_9023. I'll attach traces.
kevin-eng-runtime: next steps: 1) keep +1 slab for 24h and monitor 2) change autoscale max burst to +2 slabs and cooldown 30s for nimble-rx-pool 3) enable hashed prefix warmup 4) send customer token rotation guidance + SDK backoff snippet.
olivia-support: here's a repro curl they used, posting for eng to sanity-check:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":256}'
```
raj-eng: reproduced 429s in local replay when QPS ~700 with cold cache. will run load test with new autoscale params.
mike-sre: pls also add monitoring alert for KV cache hit drop >10% and queue depth >50k per pool.
kevin-eng-runtime: noted. I'll patch the monitor and add dashboard panel.
anna-product: assigned to customer success to coordinate credit and post-mortem.
olivia-support: customer updated: thank you — will wait 24h and report. sending them the warmup guide & token rotation tips. :thumbsup:
kevin-eng-runtime: leaving action items: raj runload-test + mike monitor + billing check + customer comms. Thanks team.
